annotations.title: Search North Carolina (NC) statutes by topic or keyword

description:
Search North Carolina (NC) statutes by topic, keyword or phrase.

Use this when you know the SUBJECT but not the citation — "what's the NC law about
leaving a dog in a hot car", "failure to appear penalty", "when can I expunge a
misdemeanor". If you already have a citation, use get_statute instead.

Returns ranked sections with highlighted fragments showing why each matched, not full
text: pick the one you want and call get_statute for it.

Supports quoted "exact phrases", -excluded terms and `or`. `match_mode` says how the
query was read: "all_terms" (every word), "all_terms_with_synonyms" (every word, but the
words as typed matched nothing or only weakly, so statutory synonyms were accepted —
"car" for "motor vehicle", "leaving" for "confined"; listed in `synonyms_used`),
"any_of" (the query used `or`), "any_terms" (nothing matched every word, so any word or
synonym was accepted) or "citation" (the query was a bare citation, so it was looked up
directly; when the section doesn't exist, the nearest real sections by number come back
as `suggestions`).
The loose modes only return sections that contain at least one of your words. Results
are ordered by `terms_matched` — how many of the search words a section contains, a
quoted phrase counting only when it appears as a phrase — then by
`catchline_terms_matched`, how many are in the section's own heading, then by
`catchline_coverage`, how much of that heading the search words make up (1.0 is an
exact title, so "DWI" finds "Impaired driving" before longer sections that merely
mention it), then by rank. Court shorthand is expanded
automatically and case-insensitively — FTA, DWLR, PJC, AWDW and similar become the
statutory wording, because the statute book spells the phrase out and never uses the
abbreviation. The expansion is reported back as `expanded_query`. Shorthand that names
one offense lists that offense's section first, marked `primary_for` (FTA → 15A-543,
DWI → 20-138.1).

Searches the law in force today, at section level. A low top rank means the corpus
probably has no section on point — NC simply has no statute on some subjects, and
saying so is a better answer than the nearest loose word match.

chapter.description: Only sections in this General Statutes chapter.

include_repealed.description: Also return repealed sections. Off by default, so results are law in force.

limit.description: Maximum number of sections to return (1-25).

query.description: Topic, keyword or phrase. Supports quoted "exact phrases", -excluded terms and `or`. Court shorthand (FTA, DWLR, PJC) is expanded for you.
